notes: §1989:A.2.12.3 AR1 makes argument-1 "a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600, in the Gregorian calendar" and states no upper limit; the upper limit of 3,067,671 is the 2023 integer date form's (§2023:15.5.2), which the row's change record calls stricter. The integer screen (CheckArgumentClasses over the Verified row, IntegerViolation) conforms at 85: a non-integer literal, a scaled item and a non-numeric argument are refused with COBOL1627. The runtime body DateOfInteger applies the 2023 ceiling at every edition (no edition arm; its conversion uses System.DateTime, which ends at year 9999), so at --std 85 an argument above 3,067,671 returns 0. The witness runs arguments 1 and 366 only. Caveat on the reading: §1989:A.2.12.4 prints the returned form as YYYYMMDD, four year digits; the verdict follows the change record and kb/Work PB5130, which read the 1989 year as bounded below only. No kb/Work note owns the fix: PB5130 covers the inverse functions INTEGER-OF-DATE and INTEGER-OF-DAY and has the same mechanism.

next.reason: 1989: argument-1 'is a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600', with no upper bound. 2023 §2023:15.22.3 AR1 requires 'a value in integer date form', which §2023:15.5.2 defines with the same meaning but adds 'shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671'. An argument above 3,067,671, in range in 1989, is now out of range (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION per §2023:15.3 AR14). Stricter. §2023:15.5.2 has no catalog row.
